mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened credit conditions and reduced near-term investment appetite.
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, no significant negative excess returns in months where FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold upward (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 1,000 above the prior month's level coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
failure_condition: In regimes where unemployment is expanding, the signal does not predict negative returns (out-of-sample t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows at a monthly rate exceeding 2% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 60-day forward return as strong supply-side momentum translates into equity optimism.
regime_hint: Economic expansion with robust manufacturing momentum
failure_condition: The effect is not statistically significant in contractionary or mixed-growth regimes (rolling IC < 0.05 over 12 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 0.5% for three consecutive months is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets deflation as a signal of monetary easing and growth potential.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < previous_month * 0.95 AND CPIAUCSL_next_month < previous_month_next * 0.95 AND CPIAUCSL_next_next_month < previous_month_next_next * 0.95
failure_condition: No significant return in periods where CPIAUCSL is trending up or where inflation is not the dominant macro variable (out-of-sample F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) crosses above 0.2 percentage points upward, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to turn positive as the labor market's tightening is interpreted as a sign of economic recovery.
failure_condition: The effect fails to materialize in periods where other labor indicators (PAYEMS) show persistent weakness (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising home sales (HOUST) above 1,200K units generate a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand and housing market optimism.
failure_condition: No effect in periods where broader consumer confidence indices (not available) are weak or GDP growth is negative (out-of-sample IV test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 1% in the same month increases the probability of a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual headwinds of supply and demand compression.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant when only one of the proxies is weak (two-tailed F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as signaled by FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to the anticipation of higher real rates and improved risk-adjusted discounting, but only when the unemployment rate is below 5.5%.
regime_hint: Monetary tightening regime with low unemployment
failure_condition: The regime-specific signal fails to predict positive returns when unemployment is rising or FEDFUNDS does not follow a clear upward path (out-of-sample event study p > 0.05).
